transcript.content: Hi, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?

Lately I keep thinking about death, and I’m starting to worry about the thoughts I’m having about not wanting to be here anymore. It's really starting to scare me, so I knew I needed to get some help.

Have you had other times in your life when you felt this depressed or had thoughts of death for at least two weeks before, or is this the first time? Did these feelings start after a specific stressful event or major change?

This is the first time I've ever felt this depressed or had thoughts of death, and it started about three weeks ago when I found out I failed a key certification exam. It just piled onto the pressure of studying for my RN-to-BSN program and working extended shifts at my understaffed clinic after the intense hurricane season.

Since this started, have you been depressed most of the day nearly every day and lost interest in almost everything, or do the feelings mainly come up when you think about failing the exam and the stress around school and work?

It’s definitely nearly every day now, not just when I think about the exam. I wake up with this heavy, hollow feeling in my chest and just go through the motions. I've also completely lost interest in things I used to love, like painting and going out to salsa with my friends.

Since this started, have you also had changes in sleep or appetite, low energy, trouble concentrating, or feelings of worthlessness or excessive guilt? If so, which ones have been happening nearly every day?

Yes, nearly every day I have almost no appetite and everything tastes like cardboard, and I'm so exhausted that I only have the energy to sit on the couch. My brain also feels incredibly foggy, making it hard to concentrate on studying or my patients, and I just feel completely useless and hollow inside. This has been going on for about three weeks now.

Have you had any experiences like hearing or seeing things other people don’t, or strongly believing something others say isn’t true? This helps me tell whether the depression may include psychotic symptoms.
No, I haven't experienced anything like that. I don't hear or see things that other people can't, and I haven't had any unusual or strong beliefs that others disagree with.
Have you had thoughts of killing yourself, and if so, have you made a specific plan or taken any steps toward it?

Yes, especially at night when I get home, I keep thinking everyone would be better off if I just didn't wake up. I haven't made a concrete plan or taken any physical steps, but I have spent time online reading about painless ways to die and picturing myself doing it. It really scares me because these thoughts are starting to feel like more than just a passing thing.

Have you ever had a period lasting several days when you felt unusually high, energized, or irritable, needed much less sleep, and were more talkative or impulsive than usual? Even if it didn’t cause problems, has anything like that ever happened to you?

No, I have never experienced a period of feeling unusually high, hyperactive, or needing less sleep. My feelings have always been the complete opposite, where I just feel very low and completely drained of energy.

final_diagnosis.reason: First lifetime depressive episode with at least 2 weeks of nearly daily depressed mood/anhedonia plus multiple neurovegetative and cognitive symptoms, including suicidal ideation, causing clear impairment. Psychotic symptoms were denied, and there is no history of mania or hypomania. Symptom severity is consistent with a severe depressive episode without psychotic symptoms.
